questions: Do line_loss_events fall to 0 with the 20 mm pitch, or does the line still drop out at the bends?
Does max_error move below 0.055 m, or does it stay pinned near 0.06 m, which would point to steering authority or lag rather than coverage?
If line losses are gone but progress is still low with off_track endings, should the track narrow to 0.09 m next?
Does steering_oscillation stay under about 0.2 with the wider bar, or does the outer sensor pair add overshoot?

intent: Test whether a 20 mm sensor pitch (span ±0.04 m) keeps the line visible at larger offsets and stops the line losses that the 15 mm bar did not fix. Only the sensor pitch changes from the iteration 1 design; track, mass, footprint and forward offset are held fixed so the result is attributable. Expected result: line_loss_events drop to 0 and max_error falls clearly below 0.06 m.
learning: Iteration 1 showed that a 15 mm pitch with a narrower track and lower mass left the failure mode unchanged (max_error at the 0.06 m floor, 1 to 2 line losses), so coverage was not the only limit. The off-track floor cannot be raised with body_width in the allowed range. The next race tests whether 20 mm pitch closes the coverage gap. If it does not, the next step is steering authority: a narrower track or a larger wheel radius.
rationale: Race evidence from the iteration 1 design (entityR2A, score 53.3955) shows all 60 trials ending off_track on every development track, with max_error of 0.062 to 0.066 m, line_loss_events of 1 to 2 and steering_oscillation of 0.07 to 0.16. Moving from 10 mm to 15 mm pitch, with the track narrowed to 0.10 m and mass to 0.7 kg, did not help: the score fell slightly from 53.612 to 53.3955. Line losses persist and max_error still sits at the 0.06 m off-track floor. The robot drifts steadily rather than oscillating, so the sensor bar is still too narrow to hold the line through the bends. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). Body_width cannot lift it above 0.06 within the allowed range (0.18 gives 0.0575), so the limit is fixed at 0.06 and I keep body_width at 0.12. I widen the sensor bar to 20 mm pitch (x = -0.04 to +0.04) while keeping the 12 mm footprint, as the Integrator's contingency rule specifies. The outer sensors then keep tape visible out to roughly 0.058 m of centre offset, so the line should not drop out before the controller can correct. Track, mass, wheel radius and forward offset stay unchanged, so this race isolates the pitch change. Expected result: line_loss_events at 0 or near it, and max_error falling below about 0.055 m with some progress gain on the s-bend.
